section_summary: This section combines U.S. military and diplomatic reporting on Japanese Army leaders, unit locations, mobilization, and preparations for possible southward operations from 1940 through July 1941. It also contains extensive translations and analyses of Japan’s revised National General Mobilization Law, National Defense Security Law, and related enforcement ordinances, emphasizing expanded economic controls, secrecy rules, espionage penalties, and prosecutorial powers. Later telegrams report troop call-ups, military transport, air-raid preparations, and Japanese activity in Indochina, Osaka, Kobe, and other strategic areas.

subfiles.title: Who’s Who in the Army: Lieutenant General Yasuji Okamura
subfiles.from: Harry I. T. Creswell, Military Attaché
subfiles.about: Biographical and professional assessment of Lieutenant General Yasuji Okamura.
subfiles.summary: Who's Who report on Lt. Gen. Yasuji Okamura: Tokyo-born, China and Manchukuo service, Shanghai Incident, Supreme Military Council in 1940, highly regarded.

subfiles.title: Who’s Who in the Army: Lieutenant General Hitoshi Imamura
subfiles.about: Career record and evaluation of Lieutenant General Hitoshi Imamura.
subfiles.summary: Who's Who report on Lt. Gen. Hitoshi Imamura of Miyagi: staff and command posts, service in England, India, Manchukuo and South China; broad-minded, spoke good English.

subfiles.title: Who’s Who in the Army: Lieutenant General Yoshio Iwamatsu
subfiles.from: Harry I. T. Creswell, Military Attaché
subfiles.about: Career history and personality assessment of Lieutenant General Yoshio Iwamatsu.
subfiles.summary: Who's Who report on Lt. Gen. Yoshio Iwamatsu: Taiwan, General Staff and Central China service before Central Air Defense Command; genial, well regarded, good war record.

subfiles.title: Who’s Who in the Army: Lieutenant General Yoshio Kozuki
subfiles.from: Harry I. T. Creswell, Military Attaché
subfiles.about: Biographical report on Lieutenant General Yoshio Kozuki and his technical and logistical career.
subfiles.summary: The report records Kozuki’s education, service in France, and numerous technical, munitions, planning, instructional, and regimental assignments. It notes his rapid promotion, appointment as chief of the Army Transportation Department, and reputation as a thorough officer capable in varied duties.

subfiles.title: Who’s Who in the Army: Lieutenant General Seitarō Uemura
subfiles.from: Harry I. T. Creswell, Military Attaché
subfiles.about: Career record of artillery officer Lieutenant General Seitarō Uemura.
subfiles.summary: Who's Who report on Lt. Gen. Seitaro Uemura: Russo-Japanese War veteran with long heavy artillery service, Manchukuo division duty and Western Air Defense Command, little known personally.

subfiles.title: Fragment of Consular Letter on Generals Itagaki and Yanagawa
subfiles.about: Final page of a consular discussion of Japanese generals’ guidance to people going to the Asian mainland.
subfiles.summary: Consular letter fragment urging Japanese emigrants to keep racial pride; Langdon says Generals Itagaki and Yanagawa's statements would sound sinister to those wanting a free China.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Naval Attaché Report on Recruiting Pilots
subfiles.from: Naval Attaché, Mexico City, via Navy Department
subfiles.about: Report that Japan had ordered two air officers to recruit pilots in the Americas.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase: the Chinese minister in Mexico says Japan sent two air-force officers to recruit Spanish refugee pilots, landing at Manzanillo, for service outside China.

subfiles.title: Navy Department Paraphrase on Japanese Pilot Recruitment
subfiles.about: Duplicate paraphrase concerning Japanese recruitment of pilots in the Americas.
subfiles.summary: Navy paraphrase repeating that two Japanese air-force officers were sent to the Americas to recruit pilots, especially Spanish refugees, landing at Manzanillo.

subfiles.title: Strictly Confidential Copy of Naval Attaché Pilot-Recruitment Report
subfiles.from: Naval Attaché, Mexico City, via Navy Department
subfiles.about: Additional copy of the intelligence report about Japanese recruitment of foreign pilots.
subfiles.summary: Strictly confidential copy of the pilot-recruitment report: orders of March 15 to two Japanese officers, with attachés to cooperate and Manzanillo the expected landing point.

subfiles.title: Fragmentary G-2 Report on a Qinghai Army Commander
subfiles.about: Fragmentary career account of an unnamed commander associated with the Qinghai Army and reorganized Second Army.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary G-2 report listing a Qinghai Army officer's brigade, division and Second Army commands; his name is not preserved.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Sugiyama’s Appointment as Army Chief of Staff
subfiles.about: Reports Prince Kan’in’s resignation and General Hajime Sugiyama’s appointment as chief of the Army General Staff.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Prince Kan'in resigned and General Sugiyama succeeded him as Army Chief of Staff, summarizing Sugiyama's career.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Government–Military Liaison Conferences
subfiles.about: Reports a decision to hold frequent conferences between senior government and military officials.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo papers announce frequent meetings of the premier and officials with Army and Navy chiefs for closer cooperation with supreme headquarters; the first has been held.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference on General Ott’s Assessment of Japan
subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a telegram concerning General Ott’s alleged criticism of Japanese military prowess.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram 1214 (November 27, 1940): Japanese officials resented General Ott's alleged report disparaging Japan's capabilities and advising against an alliance.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference on Army and Navy Demands
subfiles.about: Cross-reference to reporting on Army and Navy demands voiced by the navy minister.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram 1248 (November 30, 1940): press calls Army and Navy demands proof of complete military cooperation with the government.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Tanaka’s Testimony for the National Defense Security Bill
subfiles.about: Reports General Tanaka’s Diet testimony explaining the objectives of the national defense security bill.
subfiles.summary: Tanaka defends the National Defense Security Bill against propaganda, espionage, communism and liberal thought, denies it targets the general population, and cites the May 15 and February 26 incidents.

subfiles.title: Report on Locations of Japanese Divisions
subfiles.to: War Department and designated intelligence recipients
subfiles.about: Provides an estimated order of battle and locations of Japanese divisions.
subfiles.summary: The report lists the believed locations of the Imperial Guard and numerous Japanese divisions in Japan, Manchuria, Korea, China, Taiwan, and adjacent regions. Independent brigades are excluded, and one or more divisional identifications are marked uncertain or doubtful. Distribution included senior War Department, presidential, Treasury, planning, and naval-intelligence offices.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Silk Exports and Army Sentiment
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations
subfiles.about: Relays A. C. Buffum’s suggestion that restricting Japanese silk sales could weaken Army chauvinism.
subfiles.summary: Buffum says Japanese acquaintances believed impeding silk exports would hurt farm families supplying the Army and might reduce chauvinism.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Withdrawing Foreign Experts from Japan
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations
subfiles.about: Records Buffum’s proposal that American companies withdraw technical experts from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Buffum argues the U.S. could persuade firms like United Engineers and Brassert to withdraw experts from Japan by speaking to them.

subfiles.title: Estimate of Japanese Forces Available for a Southern Attack
subfiles.about: Estimates the Japanese forces and warning time likely for attacks on British or Dutch possessions.
subfiles.summary: Estimate that Japan could use five divisions at once, perhaps seventeen if China collapsed and Soviet agreement allowed withdrawals, with an attack possible within three or four weeks and Singapore's loss critical.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Summary of the Revised National General Mobilization Law
subfiles.about: Summarizes Tokyo despatch 5483 and revisions to Japan’s National General Mobilization Law.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs summary: revisions to the National General Mobilization Law broaden economic control, with Article 18 backing a New Economic Structure and penalties up to ten years and 50,000 yen.

subfiles.title: Despatch 5483: Revision of the National General Mobilization Law
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits and analyzes amendments to Japan’s National General Mobilization Law.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 5483: twenty-two of fifty articles of the mobilization law amended, enlarging control and penalties, tied to the New Economic Structure; passed without amendment.

subfiles.title: Enclosure to Despatch 5483: Amended Articles of the National General Mobilization Law
subfiles.from: Government of Japan, translated by the American Embassy
subfiles.about: Provides translated texts of the articles amended by Law No. 19.
subfiles.summary: The translated provisions authorize extensive control over labor, materials, capital, land, mining and water rights, enterprises, prices, and industry-wide control organizations. They establish compensation procedures while empowering the government to compel mergers, transfers, suspensions, and adherence to control agreements. The amendments also prescribe substantially increased criminal penalties, corporate liability, secrecy obligations, and anti-bribery provisions for officers of economic-control bodies.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Summary of the National Defense Security Law
subfiles.about: Summarizes the scope and probable consequences of Japan’s National Defense Security Law.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs summary: the National Defense Security Law is extremely broad, threatens embassy, consular and press reporting, reaches extraterritorially, and gives procurators wide powers.

subfiles.title: Despatch 5494: Transmitting the National Defense Security Law
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits and analyzes the text of Japan’s National Defense Security Law.
subfiles.summary: Grew explains the law’s broad definition of state secrets and its severe penalties for disclosure, foreign transmission, or collection of information deemed harmful to national defense. He warns that Article 8 could encompass ordinary information gathering and cites the resignation of an Embassy translator who feared violating it. The despatch details prosecutors’ exceptional investigative powers, restrictions on defense counsel, accelerated trials, and application throughout Japan Proper, Korea, Taiwan, and Karafuto.

subfiles.title: Enclosure to Despatch 5494: Text of the National Defense Security Law
subfiles.from: Government of Japan, translated by the American Embassy
subfiles.about: Full translation of Japan’s National Defense Security Law and its special criminal procedures.
subfiles.summary: Chapter I defines state secrets and creates offenses involving disclosure, collection, foreign transmission, economic disruption, incitement, conspiracy, and attempted violations, with punishments reaching death or life servitude. Chapter II extends special procedures to many military, security, communications, customs, and public-order laws and grants prosecutors broad powers of arrest, detention, search, seizure, and examination. It limits counsel, restricts appeals and jury trials, accelerates proceedings, and provides special jurisdictional adaptations for Korea and Taiwan.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Note on Enforcement Ordinances
subfiles.about: Notes receipt of translations of ordinances enforcing the National Defense Security Law.
subfiles.summary: Note on Tokyo despatch 5584 (May 8, 1941) with translations of enforcement ordinances for a law already reviewed within the Division.

subfiles.title: Despatch 5584: Enforcement Ordinances for the National Defense Security Law
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits translations of Imperial Ordinances Nos. 541 and 542 implementing the security law.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that the ordinances would bring the National Defense Security Law into force on May 10, 1941. They empower competent ministers to prescribe safeguards for state secrets, require special labels on secret documents, and provide for notification and label removal when information is no longer secret.

subfiles.title: Enclosure to Despatch 5584: Imperial Ordinances Nos. 541 and 542
subfiles.from: Government of Japan, translated by the American Embassy
subfiles.about: Translation of ordinances setting the effective date and administrative rules for the National Defense Security Law.
subfiles.summary: Ordinance 541 sets May 10, 1941, as the law’s effective date. Ordinance 542 directs ministers and conference heads to establish measures for guarding state secrets, requires labels on secret documents, and orders notice and removal of labels once secrecy is no longer necessary. The accompanying label diagrams were not translated.

subfiles.title: Hanoi Telegram on Movements of Generals Sumita and Nishimura
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese command movements interpreted as possible signs of a new development in Indochina.
subfiles.summary: Hanoi: General Sumita left and General Nishimura canceled a southern Indochina trip; the military cabinet chief is worried but stresses Japanese caution about new adventures.

subfiles.title: Hanoi Telegram on Japanese Command Changes and Possible Southern Bases
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese officers’ travel and speculation about an attack on the Netherlands East Indies.
subfiles.summary: Hanoi: Sumita and Nishimura head for Tokyo, Yamada replacing Nishimura; the cabinet chief expects new developments and bases in southern Indochina if the Netherlands East Indies is attacked.

subfiles.title: Information Copy on Yellow-Fever Inoculations in the Japanese Army
subfiles.about: Reports confirmation that limited numbers of Japanese Army personnel received yellow-fever inoculations.
subfiles.summary: Secret message: yellow-fever inoculations were being given to a limited number of Japanese Army personnel; more detail expected.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram on Rumored Call-Up of Reservists
subfiles.about: Reports persistent but unconfirmed rumors of Japanese reserve mobilization.
subfiles.summary: Foreign circles in Tokyo report certain reservists being called up; scope and purpose unknown, and the attaché considers it a natural precaution.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram Relaying Osaka Report on Large-Scale Troop Concentration
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, relaying Allison in Osaka
subfiles.about: Reports extensive reserve call-ups, transportation controls, and military activity in the Osaka–Kyoto area.
subfiles.summary: Allison reports the Osaka district's largest troop concentration since the China conflict began, with canceled events, no skilled stevedores for an American freighter, banned foreign-language calls, and widespread gloom.

subfiles.title: Hanoi Telegram on Uneasiness and Japanese Movements toward Southern Indochina
subfiles.about: Reports mounting concern that Japan would demand bases in southern Indochina and describes movements of Japanese matériel.
subfiles.summary: Hanoi circles expect a Japanese move south, perhaps demanding southern Indochina bases; aircraft, guns, tanks and trucks are being shipped out of Tonkin.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram Relaying Kobe Report on Military Transport and Travel Restrictions
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, relaying Warner in Kobe
subfiles.about: Reports military equipment movements, requisitioned horses, Axis shipping activity, and restrictions on foreign travel.
subfiles.summary: Warner reports anti-aircraft guns and equipment moving through Kobe, horses taken for the Army, and foreigners barred from rail travel to Shimonoseki and Nagasaki and Inland Sea boats.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram Relaying Osaka Report on Air-Raid and Transport Preparations
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, relaying Allison in Osaka
subfiles.about: Reports evacuation preparations, forced road labor, and troop movements in and near Osaka.
subfiles.summary: Osaka report: Juso residents ordered ready to evacuate to Mino, Itami neighborhood associations to supply road labor, and troops and troop trains moving toward the harbor and south.
